text:
maria (infra): Heads-up — saw a cluster-level jump in NVIDIA Xid 48/79 across a10 nodes in eu-west-3 over the last 12h. Putting quick notes + raw snippets here for triage.

ops-bot: ALERT: Xid 79 spike detected on cluster eu-west-3-gpu-pool — 38 events in last 60m :warning:

maria (infra): rough pattern: 1) most events on machines with mixed small-batch embedder workloads, 2) higher on nodes with >70% PCIe utilization, 3) coincident with nightly tenant requeue wave.

kai (sre): can you paste nvml logs + the process list around an event? even a sample will help correlate.

maria (infra): sure — here's a sanitized sample from /var/log/nvidia-events.log (trimmed):
```
[2025-10-02T03:14:12Z] Xid 79  GPU 2  pid=22844  proc=embedder_runner  tenant=cohort-A  pcie_tx=78%  ecc_uncorrectable=0
[2025-10-02T03:14:12Z] Xid 48  GPU 2  pid=22844  proc=embedder_runner  tenant=cohort-A  seq=decoding
```

rahul (ml-infra): interesting — small-batch embedder + decode path. We instrumented the low-level decoder last month; can you check KV cache sizes and model shard placement for those PIDs?

maria (infra): KV cache hit rate was ~22% for that tenant during the window. Model sharding: 2-shard split across GPUs 1/2.

kai (sre): quick hypotheses: 1) PCIe saturation causing transient DMA errors -> Xid 79, 2) memory ECC? you reported ecc_uncorrectable=0 here but need long tail checks, 3) driver/kernel mismatch on a subset of hosts.

sylvie (oncall): FYI I just soft-drained node eu3-a10-112 and saw Xid events stop for 40m. After reenable they resumed. Suggests workload-triggered not purely hardware-dead. :thinking:

maria (infra): I ran `nvidia-smi diag --query-gpu=memory.used,utilization.gpu,pcie.tx` around events. snippet:
```
GPU 2: memory.used=8.2GB util=91% pcie_tx=79%
GPU 2 pre-event: ECC_SBE=5 ECC_DBE=0
```

rahul (ml-infra): the embedder does lots of small decode calls which create noisy PCIe bursts. On a10s we've seen a correlation between lots of 1-8 token batches and Xid 48 in lab. Could be driver not handling rapid small DMA ops well.

kai (sre): action items proposal: 1) increase telemetry retention for nvml/event logs for affected nodes (48h -> 7d), 2) add per-tenant small-batch counter to metrics (batches <8 tokens), 3) run controlled repro on staging with same driver/kernel.

maria (infra): +1. I'll spin a staging repro using tenant replay and ramp small-batch ratio. Also we should snapshot driver version on nodes with events: `cat /proc/driver/nvidia/version`.

ops-bot: NOTE: new task created — TICKET-3491: Xid 48/79 correlation & repro (assignee: rahul).

sylvie (oncall): cost tradeoff question — if repro confirms workload-triggered flakiness, do we prefer preemptive soft-drain (higher scheduling pressure) or replace hardware? Replacement costs ~ $2.5k/node but soft-drain increases latency and capacity ops. Thoughts?

rahul (ml-infra): we should consider device-level heuristics: if a node has >=3 distinct Xid79 events in 24h AND batch-profile shows >60% small-batch ops, mark for temporary replacement path = soft-drain for 4h then monitor; escalate to replacement only if persistent. That reduces unnecessary HW replacements.

kai (sre): agree. Also we can add a quick kernel patch test on a canary host: bump driver to 525.x -> 535.x on a single rack and run load. If spike drops, plan a rolling driver upgrade for pool.

maria (infra): telemetry changes I'll submit in a small PR: - extend nvml log retention, - emit metric `gpu.small_batch_rate` per node, - tag Xid events with tenant and op-type in logs.

rahul (ml-infra): for repro config I'll share a containerized harness (replay + small-batch mixer). Expected runtime ~ 2h. I'll trigger after the driver-canary is up.

kai (sre): quick checklist for triage run: `1) reproduce on canary 2) capture nvml + dmesg 3) collect pcie counters 4) try driver rollback/upgrades` — copy this into the ticket.

maria (infra): copied. assigning 1st pass to rahul, canary driver upgrade to kai, monitoring PR to me. Will post updates here. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
